title: Why is snow white?
examples: Teacher, why does snow look so white?
What makes snow reflect light so well?
Does the shape of snow change how white it is?

explain.say: Snow is made of tiny, tiny pieces of ice.
These tiny pieces are called ice crystals when they fall.
When light hits these crystals, it bounces in many directions.
This bouncing of light is what makes snow look so very bright and white.
Think about a playground on a sunny day.
A common mistake is thinking snow is always the same color.

faq.a: Snow is white because its tiny ice crystals scatter all the colors of light equally. This makes it look bright white to our eyes.

faq.q: Does the shape of the snow matter?
faq.a: Yes, the shape of the ice crystals helps them scatter the light very well. Different shapes can change how much light bounces off.

faq.q: Can snow look white even if it is dirty?
faq.a: No, if snow gets dirty, it will absorb some colors of light and look grey or brown. Clean snow scatters all the light.
asks: Why is dirty snow not white?

faq.q: Is the light scattering the only reason it is white?
faq.a: While scattering is the main reason, the pure white color of the ice crystals also helps. They are very reflective materials.

faq.q: Does the sun's strength change how white the snow is?
faq.a: The strength of the sun changes how much light hits the snow, but the scattering property of the crystals remains. More light means more visible scattering.
asks: Does the sun make snow whiter?
Can snow look different in different light?

facts: Snow is made up of many small ice crystals.
These crystals are very good at scattering sunlight.
Scattering light makes the snow appear bright white.
If snow gets dirty, it will absorb some light and change color.

quiz.say: Snow appears white because the ice crystals:
quiz.why: Scattering means the light bounces in many directions, making it look white.

wrong.0: If it only reflected blue, the snow would look blue.
wrong.1: Passing light through would make it look transparent.
wrong.3: This would make the snow look black or dark.

quiz.say: If snow gets covered with dirt, it will look:
quiz.why: Dirt absorbs some colors of light, so the snow cannot scatter all colors perfectly.

wrong.0: Dirt changes the surface properties, so the color changes.
wrong.2: Dirt makes the surface rougher, which reduces perfect scattering.
wrong.3: The dirt does not change the basic scattering mechanism.

quiz.say: What is the main reason snow is white?
quiz.why: The process of scattering light is the key scientific reason for the white appearance.

wrong.0: This would only explain one color, not the overall white.
wrong.1: Temperature affects the state, but not the color from light scattering.
wrong.3: While it is ice, the 'why white' part is the light interaction.
